source: MAFF/GDAHP regulatory framework on animal feed and veterinary drug registration (compiled from USDA GAIN attache reports and FAO/GDAHP sources)
text:
Cambodia has a real, legally-required registration system for animal feed, feed ingredients, feed additives, and veterinary drugs, administered by the General Directorate of Animal Health and Production (GDAHP) under MAFF. Companies that produce, import, or sell these products are legally required to register with the government and obtain a permit before selling. GDAHP has a dedicated registration committee (established under Prakas No. 368) responsible for reviewing and licensing feed and veterinary drug services. As of 2025, the government has also been developing specific regulation for 'medicated feed' (feed containing veterinary drugs, such as antibiotics), working with FAO, specifically to prevent misuse and drug residues and to secure safe, high-quality feed.

What this means practically for a farmer buying feed: legitimate, registered feed products should come from licensed dealers and carry proper packaging and labeling, since registration is a real legal requirement, not just a suggestion. Practical steps to reduce risk when buying feed: buy from an established, licensed feed dealer rather than unmarked or informal sources; be cautious of feed sold without any packaging, labeling, or company information; be skeptical of pricing that seems unusually cheap compared to other sellers, which can be a sign of an unregistered or adulterated product; and if unsure, ask the local agricultural or livestock extension officer (District/Provincial Office of Animal Health and Production) to confirm whether a specific product or supplier is registered, since they have access to the official registration list that individual farmers do not.
